# docstore

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/docstore"
```

Package docstore is the public facade for the SDK's document store: typed, keyed JSON documents with unique and multi-valued secondary indexes, kept in memory or persisted to a filesystem, every write durable before it returns.

```
type Account struct {
    ID    string   `json:"id"`
    Email string   `json:"email"`
    Teams []string `json:"teams"`
}

data, err := vfs.NewOS("/var/lib/app") // or vfs.NewMem(), or nil FS for memory
accounts, err := docstore.Open(
    docstore.Config[Account]{
        Key:  func(a Account) string { return a.ID },
        FS:   data,
        Path: "members/accounts.json",
    },
    docstore.Unique("email", func(a Account) string { return a.Email }),
    docstore.Index("team", func(a Account) []string { return a.Teams }),
)
defer accounts.Close()

err = accounts.Insert(Account{ID: "acc_1", Email: "ada@example.com"})
ada, err := accounts.Lookup("email", "ada@example.com")
red, err := accounts.Find("team", "red")
```

### Documents, keys and the write modes

A document is kept as its JSON encoding, so every read returns a copy and a caller can never alias what the store holds. Its key is what [Config](#Config).Key returns; an empty key is refused. Put creates or replaces; Insert refuses a key that is taken (DocumentExists); Replace refuses a key that is not (DocumentNotFound), so a document deleted meanwhile is never brought back. Update applies a function to a copy and stores the result atomically with respect to every other write — its function may read the store, and must not write to it. Delete removes.

### Indexes

[Unique](#Unique) files at most one document per key: a write that would file a second is refused with UniqueKeyTaken and changes nothing. [Index](#Index) files any number. Empty keys are not indexed. Lookup reads a unique index; Find reads any index, in store-key order, and answers an empty slice rather than an error; Filter reads every document. The indexes are rebuilt when the store opens, and documents that break a unique index refuse the open (IndexBroken) rather than answer lies.

No refusal ever quotes a key: a store key is routinely an e-mail address, an index key the hash of a token.

### How it persists, and what a write costs

At rest the store is ONE file, the snapshot — a JSON object from key to document, the file a person can open. A write publishes one small file beside it, in the directory Path + ".d", atomically, before it returns — so a write costs one document, whatever the store holds. When that overlay holds as many entries as the store holds documents (at least [DefaultFoldAt](#DefaultFoldAt)), the write that got it there folds it back into the snapshot: one rewrite per N writes, a constant on average. Close folds too. Opening replays the overlay over the snapshot, and a crash at any point of a fold loads the same documents. BENCH.md in internal/service/data/docstore has the numbers: a write at 100 000 documents costs what it costs at 100, where rewriting the whole file costs 70 ms.

A publication that fails is PersistFailed and changes nothing. One whose rename happened but whose directory flush failed is WriteUnconfirmed: the write stands — the file shows it, and so does the store — and only its survival across a power loss is in doubt.

### Concurrency, and what it is not

A Store is safe for concurrent use, and a reader never waits for a disk: writers are serialised among themselves and do their filesystem work alone, and the documents change only once a write is durable. OnWrite and OnDelete tell a caller about each write once it is durable, outside every lock.

It is one process's store: a second process opening the same files is not detected. It keeps every document in memory. It has no transaction across documents. It is a store for the documents a service owns, not a database.

### Consistency

The two engines state what a read after a write returns, and it is not the same. A [Store](#Store) is read-your-writes within the process: once a write has returned, every call of the process reads it, and a reader never waits — it sees the store before a write or after it, never between. A [SQLStore](#SQLStore) reads at the isolation of the transaction a call runs on: a write is visible to its own transaction at once, and to every other one once it commits — never before, never if it rolls back — and a caller inside a REPEATABLE READ transaction reads its snapshot. A call on the pool is a transaction of its own and reads what is committed.

### The same store over SQL

[OpenSQL](#OpenSQL) keeps the same documents — the same keys, indexes, write modes, hooks and refusals, the same codes — in two tables of a PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite database the caller opened and hands over as a \[sql.Transactor]. Nothing is held in memory: the database is the source of truth, and every call is a round trip that takes a context (ADR 0139).

```
tm, err := sql.NewTransactor(sql.Config{DB: pool, Dialect: sql.DialectPostgres, Pool: sql.PoolConfig{MaxOpen: 10}})
create, err := docstore.SQLMigration(sql.DialectPostgres, "members__accounts", 20260927120000) // run by your Migrator
accounts, err := docstore.OpenSQL(
    docstore.SQLConfig[Account]{Key: func(a Account) string { return a.ID },
        Transactor: tm, Dialect: sql.DialectPostgres, Table: "members__accounts"},
    docstore.Unique("email", func(a Account) string { return a.Email }),
)
err = sql.Transact(ctx, tm, func(ctx context.Context, _ sql.Executor) error {
    return accounts.Insert(ctx, Account{ID: "acc_1", Email: "ada@example.com"}) // joins this transaction
})
```

A call runs on the transaction its context carries for that transactor, and on the pool otherwise. A write runs in a savepoint of the caller's transaction — or a transaction of its own — so it is atomic on its own, and a refused or failed one leaves the caller's transaction usable. Its hooks run once the transaction that holds it has committed, and never for one rolled back.

The document is kept as the bytes the store encoded, never as the engine's JSON type, which reorders members and respells numbers, so it reads back byte for byte. Keys are compared as bytes — binary key columns, no collation — so "a", "A" and "a " are three keys, as they are in Go. A key longer than [MaxSQLKeyLen](#MaxSQLKeyLen) bytes is refused with KeyTooLong. Index keys may reach the table hashed: [SQLConfig](#SQLConfig).IndexKey transforms every one at a write and at every Lookup and Find, and an index is an equality lookup, which a keyed hash keeps. Index rows are kept, not rebuilt at every open: after a declaration changes, [SQLStore](#SQLStore).Reindex files the stored documents again.

A failure of the database is StatementFailed, which a caller answers with a 503: the driver's error is joined beside it for errors.Is and errors.As, and withheld from its text, because a driver quotes the row a constraint refused and that row holds a key.

### The ports, for a double

[Store](#Store) and [SQLStore](#SQLStore) are engines. A caller that must stand a double in for one depends instead on the port it implements: [Collection](#Collection), [Versioned](#Versioned), [Trashable](#Trashable), [KeyLister](#KeyLister), [VersionWriter](#VersionWriter) and [VersionWeigher](#VersionWeigher) for a [Store](#Store), whose calls take no context, [CollectionContext](#CollectionContext), [VersionedContext](#VersionedContext), [TrashableContext](#TrashableContext), [KeyListerContext](#KeyListerContext), [VersionWriterContext](#VersionWriterContext) and [VersionWeigherContext](#VersionWeigherContext) for a [SQLStore](#SQLStore), whose every call takes one, and [Announcer](#Announcer) — OnWrite and OnDelete — for either. Each pair carries the same methods, the same documents and the same refusals; there is no single port over both, because the file engine waits on nothing a context could abandon while the SQL engine waits on a database (ADR 0160).

### Versions

A store opened with [Config](#Config).Versions — or [SQLConfig](#SQLConfig).Versions — keeps the last versions of each document, as a content system keeps a page's revisions (ADR 0143):

```
pages, err := docstore.Open(docstore.Config[Page]{Key: Page.Key, FS: data, Path: "cms/pages.json", Versions: 20})
err = pages.PutStamped(page, docstore.Stamp{Meta: map[string]string{"by": userID, "command": "pages.Edit"}})
revisions, err := pages.Versions(page.ID) // newest first: the page as it is, then the 20 before it
third, err := pages.Version(page.ID, revisions[3].Number)
```

A creation is version 1, and every write that changes the document makes the next one, stamped with the instant of [Config](#Config).Clock and the metadata the Stamped writes carry — who, which command; the plain writes carry none. A number is never given twice while the document exists. A write storing the JSON already stored makes no version, and neither does one stamped InPlace: the document changes and its current version keeps its number. The former versions beyond Versions are pruned by the write that makes a newer one, in the same durable write as the document — the same overlay entry, the same transaction — so no crash ever leaves the versions ahead of or behind their document. [Config](#Config).Held keeps a document's versions from pruning, for a legal hold, until a write finds it released. RewriteVersions rewrites a document's former versions under the writers' lock, for an erasure: it may clear or drop them, never renumber or add one. A deletion takes every version with it. Versions are never indexed: Lookup and Find read the current version.

The file store keeps them in memory, in each write's overlay entry and, at rest, in the file Path + ".versions"; a store opened without versions over files that keep them is refused, rather than left to drop them. The SQL store keeps them in a third table, which [SQLVersionsMigration](#SQLVersionsMigration) creates. [Version](#Version).JSON is compact JSON; a version predating a change of the type may no longer decode into it, which is why it is JSON and not a T.

### The trash

A store that keeps versions has a trash (ADR 0143, amended for ADR 0178):

```
err = pages.Trash(page.ID)            // gone from Get, List, Lookup and Find; its versions stay
trash, err := pages.Tombstones()      // every trashed key, with when it was trashed
err = pages.Restore(page.ID)          // back as it was, filed again
err = pages.Purge(page.ID)            // or gone for good, its versions with it
```

A trashed document leaves every read and frees its unique keys, as a former version does; Versions still reads what it kept, the trashed document first. Its number is kept: a creation under its key is a write over the trashed document, which continues its versions. Restore brings it back exactly as it was, or refuses with UniqueKeyTaken when another document took one of its unique keys meanwhile. Purge removes it and its versions. Delete never reaches the trash: it takes a document and its versions at once, which is what an erasure needs, and finds no trashed document. How long a document stays in the trash is the caller's to decide; the store empties nothing by itself.

### What the versions weigh

VersionWeight says what a store keeps beyond its documents — for a page that shows what a history costs (ADR 0143):

```
w, err := pages.VersionWeight() // w.Former versions and w.Trashed documents, w.Bytes of JSON
```

A document's current version is the document itself and is not counted. [Store](#Store) keeps the weight as a counter every write moves — Stats reports it too — so asking reads no version; [SQLStore](#SQLStore) asks its database one aggregate statement over the versions table, which sends back one row. The same writes weigh the same on both.

### Keys

Keys lists the keys of the documents a store holds, in key order, and reads no document — for a caller that must visit every record, a re-scan after a crash, without paying for what the records weigh (ADR 0178):

```
for key, err := range pages.Keys("") {
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	…
}
```

[Store](#Store) sorts the keys it holds once, when the range starts; [SQLStore](#SQLStore) reads them in pages on the primary key, each resuming after the last key read. Both resume after the key a caller names, so a listing stopped early continues where it stopped. A document in the trash is not listed: Keys lists what Get finds.

<a name="Index"></a>
## func [Index](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Index[T any](name string, keys func(T) []string) IndexSpec[T]
```

Index declares an index where a document may have several keys and a key several documents. Empty keys are not indexed.

<a name="Open"></a>
## func [Open](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Open[T any](cfg Config[T], indexes ...IndexSpec[T]) (*Store[T], error)
```

Open builds a store from cfg with the secondary indexes given: in memory without a filesystem, otherwise loaded from it — the snapshot, the overlay replayed on top, the indexes rebuilt. It creates the directories the store lives in, 0700, and writes its files 0600.

<a name="OpenSQL"></a>
## func [OpenSQL](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func OpenSQL[T any](cfg SQLConfig[T], indexes ...IndexSpec[T]) (*SQLStore[T], error)
```

OpenSQL builds a store over SQL from cfg with the secondary indexes given, declared as for [Open](#Open). It sends no statement: its tables are [SQLMigration](#SQLMigration)'s, run by the caller's Migrator before the store is used.

<a name="Ordered"></a>
## func [Ordered](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Ordered[T any](name string, key func(T) string) IndexSpec[T]
```

Ordered declares an index over the one key key returns that keeps its keys in order, for Range: keys compare as bytes, so pad a number and write an instant in RFC 3339, in UTC. An empty key is not indexed.

<a name="SQLMigration"></a>
## func [SQLMigration](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func SQLMigration(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
```

SQLMigration returns the migration that creates the two tables a SQL store named table keeps on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version table. Its Down drops both, and every document in them. Every statement does nothing when its table exists, so a run MySQL's implicit commit stopped halfway completes when it runs again. Its Checksum fingerprints Up's statements, so a version table that recorded it refuses a build whose statements differ.

<a name="SQLVersionsMigration"></a>
## func [SQLVersionsMigration](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func SQLVersionsMigration(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
```

SQLVersionsMigration returns the migration that creates the table a SQL store named table keeps its versions in on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version table, beside [SQLMigration](#SQLMigration)'s. A store opened with [SQLConfig](#SQLConfig).Versions needs it. Its Down drops the table, and every version in it: run it to turn versions off for good. Its Checksum fingerprints Up's statements, so a version table that recorded it refuses a build whose statements differ.

<a name="SQLVersionsTrashIndexMigration"></a>
## func [SQLVersionsTrashIndexMigration](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func SQLVersionsTrashIndexMigration(dialect sql.Dialect, table string, version uint64) (sql.Migration, error)
```

SQLVersionsTrashIndexMigration returns the migration that indexes the trash of a SQL store named table on dialect, numbered version for the caller's own version table, after [SQLVersionsMigration](#SQLVersionsMigration)'s: Tombstones then reads the trash alone instead of every version. Up and Down do nothing when there is nothing to do, and touch no version.

<a name="Announcer"></a>
## type [Announcer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Announcer is the public alias for the pair of hooks both engines answer exactly as they are: OnWrite and OnDelete.

```go

```

Announcer is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.Announcer`, declared as:

```go
type Announcer interface {
	// OnDelete registers fn to be told the key of every document Delete or
	// Trash removed, on the same terms as OnWrite.
	OnDelete(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
	// OnWrite registers fn to be told the key of every document Put, Insert,
	// Replace, Update or Restore stored, and returns the function that removes
	// the registration. A nil fn registers nothing. A panic in fn reaches the
	// writer after its write stood.
	OnWrite(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
}
```


<a name="Announcer.OnWrite"></a>


## type [Batcher](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Batcher is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection](#Collection) that writes several documents as one without a context, which [Store](#Store) implements: Batch — every write, or none.

```go

```

Batcher is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.Batcher`, declared as:

<a name="Batcher.Batch"></a>
### func \(Batcher\) [Batch](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/docstore/gen_ports.go>)

```go

```

Batch runs fn with a [BatchWriter](#BatchWriter), then writes what it recorded, in order, as one: every write, or none when one is refused — the refusal returned, nothing changed — and none when fn returns an error, which Batch returns as it is. A write makes its version and files its index keys as it would alone; OnWrite and OnDelete are told about each write once the whole batch took effect, in order. fn runs before any lock: it may read the store, and its writes wait for the batch.

<a name="Collection.Update"></a>

```go

```

Update applies fn to a copy of the document stored under key and stores the result, atomically with respect to every other write, and returns it. <a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Config is the public alias for a store's configuration: Key (required), FS and Path (both, or neither for a memory store), FoldAt, Versions with its Clock and Held, and the change feed Changes with ChangesWithDocument.

```go
type Config[T any] = svcdocstore.Config[T]
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/docstore.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config[T any] struct {
	// Key returns the key a document is stored under. It must be a pure
	// function of the document: the store calls it to file every write and
	// compares its answers to refuse an update that would rename a document.
	Key                 func(T) string
	// FS is where the store persists, and Path is the snapshot's name inside
	// it — an io/fs name such as "shop/items.json". The overlay lives beside
	// the snapshot, in the directory Path + ".d". A nil FS keeps the store in
	// memory: nothing survives the process, and nothing is written anywhere.
	FS                  corevfs.FullFS
	// Clock stamps each version with the instant of the write that made it.
	// Nil is the system clock.
	Clock               clock.Clock
	// Held reports whether the document stored under key is held — a legal
	// hold — so that no write prunes its versions: they pile up beyond
	// Versions until a write finds the document released, and that write
	// prunes them. It is called with the document's key by a write that would
	// prune, under the writers' lock, so it may read this store and must not
	// write to it; a panic in it reaches the writer, and nothing is written.
	// Nil holds nothing. It is refused without Versions.
	Held                func(key string) bool
	// Path is the snapshot's name inside FS. It is required with FS and
	// refused without it, because a path with nowhere to be written is a
	// store that would silently keep nothing.
	Path                string
	// FoldAt is how many overlay entries fold the overlay into the snapshot
	// on the write that reaches it. Zero is the default rule: as many entries
	// as the store holds documents, and at least [DefaultFoldAt]. A negative
	// value never folds on a write; Fold, Open and Close still do.
	FoldAt              int
	// Versions is how many former versions each document keeps beside its
	// current one, the newest: a write that changes a document makes a new
	// version, and prunes the oldest beyond Versions in the same durable
	// write. Zero keeps no versions — the store writes exactly the files it
	// wrote before versions existed — and a negative value is refused. A
	// persistent store keeps them in the file Path + ".versions" once a fold
	// ran, and a store opened with zero over files that keep versions is
	// refused rather than left to drop or corrupt them (ADR 0143). A store
	// that keeps versions has a trash, Trash's; one that keeps none has none.
	Versions            int
	// Changes is the store's change feed (kitsunium/sdk#831): every write
	// that stands appends one record to it — keyed by the document's key,
	// its payload a [coredocstore.ChangeValue] as JSON — under the
	// writers' lock and BEFORE the write's overlay entry is published, so
	// the records of a key are in the order its writes stood. A crash
	// between the two leaves a record of a write that did not land: the
	// feed is at least once, and a reader skips a record whose version
	// the store does not hold. A publication the store refuses is
	// answered by a record that restates the key as it stands — put,
	// trash or delete. A record the stream refuses refuses the
	// write, ChangeFeedFailed, nothing written. A batch appends one record
	// per key it wrote, its final state. Nil writes no
	// record.
	Changes             corestream.Stream
	// ChangesWithDocument puts the document's JSON in each change record
	// of a put, a restore and a trash, so a reader rebuilds the store from
	// the feed alone. It is refused without Changes.
	ChangesWithDocument bool
}
```

<a name="SQLConfig"></a>
## type [SQLConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

SQLConfig is the public alias for a SQL store's configuration: Key, Transactor, Dialect and Table (required), IndexKey, Versions with its Clock and Held, and the change feed Changes with ChangesWithDocument.

```go
type SQLConfig[T any] = svcdocstore.SQLConfig[T]
```

SQLConfig is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/docstore.SQLConfig`, declared as:

```go
type SQLConfig[T any] struct {
	// Key returns the key a document is stored under, as for [Open]: a pure
	// function of the document, compared byte for byte.
	Key                 func(T) string
	// Clock stamps each version with the instant of the write that made it.
	// Nil is the system clock.
	Clock               clock.Clock
	// Held reports whether the document stored under key is held — a legal
	// hold — so that no write prunes its versions, as for [Open]. It is
	// called by a write that would prune, inside that write's transaction
	// and with its context, so a read it makes through the same transactor
	// joins it. Nil holds nothing. It is refused without Versions.
	Held                func(ctx context.Context, key string) bool
	// Transactor is the transaction manager of the database the store lives
	// in — the one the caller's own transactions are opened with, so a call
	// made under one of them joins it. It must also be a core/data/sql Joiner and
	// Deferrer, which the SDK's own transactor is.
	Transactor          coresql.Transactor
	// IndexKey, when set, transforms every index key before it reaches the
	// database — on a write, and on every Lookup and Find — so a table holds
	// what it returns and never the key itself. An index is an equality
	// lookup, which a keyed hash keeps: a framework passes an HMAC under a key
	// of its own, and an e-mail address never reaches a table. It is called
	// with the index's name and a non-empty key; an empty answer files
	// nothing, as an empty key does. Nil stores index keys as they are. An
	// ordered index's keys, and Range's bounds, go through it too: Range
	// compares them as the table holds them, so a transform that does not
	// keep their order — a keyed hash — leaves Range no order to read;
	// return an ordered index's key as it is.
	IndexKey            func(index string, key string) []byte
	// Table names the documents' table. The store derives its index table's
	// name from it by appending "___ix". It is a lower-case SQL identifier of
	// at most [MaxSQLTableLen] bytes, holds no three underscores in a row,
	// and does not start with "sqlite_". [SQLMigration] creates both tables.
	Table               string
	// Dialect is the engine's: the SQL the store speaks to it. It must be the
	// Transactor's own.
	Dialect             coresql.Dialect
	// Versions is how many former versions each document keeps beside its
	// current one, as for [Open]: a write that changes a document makes a
	// new version and prunes the oldest beyond Versions, in its own
	// transaction. They live in a third table, <Table>___vs, which
	// [SQLVersionsMigration] creates. Zero keeps no versions and sends
	// exactly the statements the store sent before versions existed; a
	// negative value is refused. The store cannot see a versions table it was
	// told nothing about: turned off, it leaves the table as it is, and a
	// document deleted and written again meanwhile would find the rows of the
	// one it replaced — so drop the table with the migration's Down (ADR 0143).
	// A store that keeps versions has a trash, Trash's, in the same table; one
	// that keeps none has none.
	Versions            int
	// Changes is the store's change feed (kitsunium/sdk#831): every write
	// appends one record to it — keyed by the document's key, its payload a
	// [coredocstore.ChangeValue] as JSON — INSIDE the write's own
	// transaction or savepoint, with the write's context, so a write rolled
	// back leaves no record and a committed one exactly one. That holds
	// when Changes is the stream's SQL engine (internal/service/data/stream
	// NewSQL) opened on this store's Transactor: on another transactor the
	// record would commit apart from the write. A record the stream refuses
	// rolls the write back, ChangeFeedFailed. With Changes every write runs
	// in a transaction, even one of one statement. Nil writes no record.
	Changes             corestream.Stream
	// ChangesWithDocument puts the document's JSON in each change record
	// of a put, a restore and a trash, so a reader rebuilds the store from
	// the feed alone. It is refused without Changes.
	ChangesWithDocument bool
}
```

<a name="SQLStore"></a>
## type [SQLStore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

SQLStore is the public alias for the document store over SQL: Get, GetInto, List, Filter, Entries, Keys, Count, Lookup and Find read, and Documents, FindAfter and Range read a page at a time; Put, Insert, Replace, Update and Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make records; Versions, Version, RewriteVersions and VersionWeight, Trash, Restore, Purge and Tombstones as for [Store](#Store); OnWrite and OnDelete announce once the write's transaction commits, and ChangeStream names the change feed; Reindex files the stored documents again. Every call takes a context.



Count returns how many documents the store holds.

```go

```

Delete removes the document stored under key, or returns DocumentNotFound. Its versions go with it, in the same transaction: a deletion never reaches the trash, which is Trash's.

<a name="SQLStore.Documents"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Documents](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_page.go>)

```go

```

Documents yields the documents whose key sorts after after, in key order, each with its key and the JSON the store wrote, at most limit of them — every one when limit is not positive. It reads them in pages of at most a few hundred, each page one statement on the primary key that resumes after the last key read, on the transaction ctx carries, else on the pool; a page is read whole and its rows closed before the first of it is yielded, so the caller may write in the loop. func (*SQLStore) Lookup(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (T, error)

Lookup returns the document holding key in the unique index named index, DocumentNotFound when none does, IndexUnknown for an undeclared index and IndexNotUnique for an index that may hold several: read that one with Find.

<a name="SQLStore.OnDelete"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [OnDelete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_store.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) OnDelete(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
```

OnDelete registers fn to be told the key of every document Delete or Trash removed, on the same terms as OnWrite.

<a name="SQLStore.OnWrite"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [OnWrite](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_store.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) OnWrite(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
```

OnWrite registers fn to be told the key of every document Put, Insert, Replace, Update or Restore stored, once the transaction that holds the write has committed — never for a write that is rolled back — on the goroutine that committed it, outside every lock. It returns the function that removes the registration.

<a name="SQLStore.Purge"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Purge](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_trash.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Purge(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Purge empties the trash of the document trashed under key: the trashed document and every version row of its key go, in one transaction, and a document written later under the key starts again at version 1. It calls no hook and asks Held nothing, as Delete does not. DocumentNotTrashed when no document is trashed under key.

<a name="SQLStore.Put"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Put](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_write.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Put(ctx context.Context, v T) error
```

Put stores v under its key, creating it or replacing whatever was there. On a store that keeps versions, it makes one, stamped with nothing.

<a name="SQLStore.PutDocument"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [PutDocument](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) PutDocument(ctx context.Context, key string, versions []coredocstore.VersionValue, trashedAt time.Time) error
```

PutDocument writes the document key with its versions as they are given, in one transaction — a savepoint of the caller's when ctx carries one —, as core/data/docstore.VersionWriterContext says: the document's row and its index rows unless it is trashed, and a version row for each version — the trash's row, numbered 0, at trashedAt when it is set. It calls OnWrite once that transaction commits, for a stored document. DocumentExists when anything is under key — a document, the trash, or version rows —, VersionsInvalid, DocumentUndecodable, KeyTooLong or UniqueKeyTaken for what cannot be written as given, VersionsNotKept on a store that keeps none; nothing changes on a refusal.

<a name="SQLStore.PutStamped"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [PutStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) PutStamped(ctx context.Context, v T, stamp coredocstore.StampValue) error
```

PutStamped is Put, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="SQLStore.Range"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Range](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_page.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Range(ctx context.Context, index string, lo string, hi string, limit int) iter.Seq2[T, error]
```

Range yields the documents filed in the ordered index named index under a key from lo, included, to hi, excluded — no upper bound when hi is empty — in index-key order, then store-key order, at most limit of them — every one when limit is not positive —, a page per statement on the index table's primary key, which resumes after the last index key and store key read; only the documents yielded are read and decoded. The bounds reach the table as an index key does, through IndexKey when one is set. IndexUnknown for an undeclared index, IndexNotOrdered for one declared without Ordered.

<a name="SQLStore.Reindex"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Reindex](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_reindex.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Reindex(ctx context.Context) error
```

Reindex rebuilds every index row from the stored documents, in one transaction — a savepoint of the caller's when ctx carries one.

The SQL store keeps its index rows, where the memory and file store rebuild theirs at every Open. So a change to the declarations — an index added, a key function or IndexKey changed, an index made unique — files nothing for the documents already stored until Reindex runs. It drops every row, including those of an index no longer declared, reads the documents in key order a page at a time, and files each one's keys again.

Documents that break a unique index refuse the rebuild with INDEX\_BROKEN, naming the index and never the key, and so does a key function that panics; a document the type no longer fits is DOCUMENT\_UNDECODABLE. Nothing changes then. Run it when no write to the store runs beside it: a write in flight files its keys under whichever rows it finds.

<a name="SQLStore.Replace"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Replace](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_write.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Replace(ctx context.Context, v T) error
```

Replace stores v over the document already under its key: DocumentNotFound when there is none, so a document deleted meanwhile is never brought back.

<a name="SQLStore.ReplaceIf"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [ReplaceIf](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_revision.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) ReplaceIf(ctx context.Context, v T, rev coredocstore.RevisionValue) error
```

ReplaceIf stores v over the document under its key, as Replace does, when the row's revision is still rev: one UPDATE conditioned on it, or — on a store that keeps versions, which reads what it replaces — the row read and locked on that condition, in the write's transaction. When nothing matched, the row is read again past the caller's snapshot: RevisionMismatch when it is there, DocumentNotFound when it is not. A revision that is not one of this engine's never matches.

<a name="SQLStore.ReplaceStamped"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [ReplaceStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) ReplaceStamped(ctx context.Context, v T, stamp coredocstore.StampValue) error
```

ReplaceStamped is Replace, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="SQLStore.Restore"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Restore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_trash.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Restore(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Restore brings the document trashed under key back exactly as it was — the same JSON, the same current version — files it again and calls OnWrite once its transaction commits. DocumentNotTrashed when no document is trashed under key, UniqueKeyTaken when another document took one of its unique keys meanwhile, DocumentUndecodable when it no longer decodes into the store's type; nothing changes on a refusal.

<a name="SQLStore.Revision"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Revision](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_revision.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Revision(ctx context.Context, key string) (T, coredocstore.RevisionValue, error)
```

Revision returns the document stored under key and its revision — the row's rev, which every write moves, in decimal — read in one statement on the transaction ctx carries, else on the pool. DocumentNotFound when no document is stored under key.

<a name="SQLStore.RewriteVersions"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [RewriteVersions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) RewriteVersions(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(former []coredocstore.VersionValue) ([]coredocstore.VersionValue, error)) error
```

RewriteVersions rewrites the former versions of the document stored under key — every version but the current one, which is the document and which only a write changes — in one transaction, a savepoint of the caller's when ctx carries one, the document locked as a write locks it. fn receives copies of them, newest first, and returns those to keep, in the same order, under the rules of [Store](#Store).RewriteVersions: VersionsRewriteRefused otherwise, and fn's own error returned as it is, nothing changed either way. It calls no hook: the document did not change.

<a name="SQLStore.Tombstones"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Tombstones](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_trash.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Tombstones(ctx context.Context) (tombstones []coredocstore.TombstoneValue, err error)
```

Tombstones returns every document in the trash, in key order: its key and the instant it was trashed, read in one statement on the transaction ctx carries. The statement scans the versions table, as List scans the documents'.

<a name="SQLStore.Trash"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Trash](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_trash.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Trash(ctx context.Context, key string) error
```

Trash moves the document stored under key to the trash, in one transaction — a savepoint of the caller's when ctx carries one: its row and its index rows go, and a version row numbered 0 — no version's number — holds the document and the instant it was trashed beside its versions, which stay. It calls OnDelete once that transaction commits. DocumentNotFound when no document is stored under key, VersionsNotKept when the store keeps no versions: only a store that keeps versions has a trash.

<a name="SQLStore.Update"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Update](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_write.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Update(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(*T) error) (T, error)
```

Update applies fn to a copy of the document stored under key and stores the result, atomically: the document is locked from the read to the write — its row on PostgreSQL and MySQL, the database's write lock on SQLite — so no other write lands between them. An error from fn changes nothing and is returned for errors.Is to find, and a result whose key is not key is DocumentKeyChanged. It returns the stored result.

fn runs inside the write's transaction. It may read the store; a read under a context carrying no transaction runs on the pool, and so needs a second connection. It must not write the document it updates, which is locked by the very write that is waiting for fn.

<a name="SQLStore.UpdateStamped"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [UpdateStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_write.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) UpdateStamped(ctx context.Context, key string, stamp coredocstore.StampValue, fn func(*T) error) (T, error)
```

UpdateStamped is Update, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="SQLStore.Version"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Version](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Version(ctx context.Context, key string, number uint64) (coredocstore.VersionValue, error)
```

Version returns the version numbered number of the document stored under key, VersionNotFound when the document keeps none of that number — never made, or pruned — and what Versions returns otherwise.

<a name="SQLStore.VersionWeight"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [VersionWeight](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) VersionWeight(ctx context.Context) (coredocstore.VersionWeightValue, error)
```

VersionWeight reports what the store keeps beyond its documents, as core/data/docstore.VersionWeigherContext says: one aggregate statement over the versions table — its former rows, its trash rows numbered 0, and the length of the documents they hold —, on the transaction ctx carries, else on the pool. The database scans the table and sends one row. VersionsNotKept on a store that keeps none, StatementFailed when the database does not answer.

<a name="SQLStore.Versions"></a>
### func \(SQLStore\) [Versions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/sql_version.go>)

```go
func (*SQLStore) Versions(ctx context.Context, key string) (versions []coredocstore.VersionValue, err error)
```

Versions returns the versions the store keeps of the document stored under key, newest first: the current one — the document as it is now — then the former ones, read in one statement on the transaction ctx carries; a document in the trash answers the versions it kept, the trashed document first, in a second one. DocumentNotFound when no document is stored or trashed under key, VersionsNotKept when the store keeps no versions.

<a name="Stamp"></a>
## type [Stamp](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Stamp is the public alias for what a Stamped write says about the version it makes: the Meta the version records, or InPlace — no version.

```go
type Stamp = coredocstore.StampValue
```

Stamp is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.StampValue`, declared as:

```go
type Stamp struct {
	// Meta is kept with the version the write makes — who made it, which
	// command — and read back with it. The store copies it and never reads
	// it.
	Meta    map[string]string
	// InPlace makes the write change the document without making a version:
	// the current version keeps its number, its instant and its Meta, and
	// holds the new document. A framework stamps so a workflow's transition,
	// which its journal already records. A creation is version 1 all the
	// same.
	InPlace bool
}
```

<a name="Stats"></a>
## type [Stats](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Stats is the public alias for what a store says about itself: documents, pending overlay entries, folds, the last automatic fold's failure, and what its versions weigh.

```go
type Stats = svcdocstore.StatsValue
```

Stats is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/docstore.StatsValue`, declared as:

```go
type Stats struct {
	// FoldError is the last automatic fold's failure, nil once a fold
	// succeeds. The write that triggered the fold succeeded either way — its
	// own entry was already durable — and the entries stay until a fold works.
	FoldError error
	// Documents is how many documents the store holds.
	Documents int
	// Pending is how many overlay entries the snapshot does not contain yet:
	// zero in memory, and after a fold.
	Pending   int
	// Folds is how many folds ran since the store opened, Open's own included.
	Folds     int
	// Versions is what the store's versions weigh — its former versions, its
	// trashed documents and their bytes —, a counter every write moves:
	// zero on a store that keeps none (ADR 0143).
	Versions  coredocstore.VersionWeightValue
}
```

<a name="Store"></a>
## type [Store](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Store is the public alias for the document store: Get, GetInto, List, Filter, Entries, Keys, Lookup, Find and Stats read, and Documents, FindAfter and Range read a page at a time; Put, Insert, Replace, Update and Delete write, and their Stamped forms say what the version they make records; Versions and Version read a document's versions, RewriteVersions rewrites its former ones, VersionWeight says what they weigh; Trash, Restore, Purge and Tombstones keep its trash; OnWrite and OnDelete announce, and ChangeStream names the change feed; Fold and Close bring it to rest.

```go
type Store[T any] = svcdocstore.Store[T]
```

Store is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/data/docstore.Store`, declared as:

```go
type Store[T any] struct{}
```

<a name="Store.Batch"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Batch](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/batch.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Batch(fn func(w coredocstore.BatchWriter[T]) error) error
```

Batch writes what fn records as one: planned under the writers' lock over the store and the batch's own writes — the first refusal ends it, nothing written — then published as ONE group entry holding every written key's latest state, then each key's own entry, then the group entry removed; a crash leaves the group entry, which the next Open replays over the keys' entries. The hooks run once it took effect.

<a name="Store.ChangeStream"></a>
### func \(Store\) [ChangeStream](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/change.go>)

```go
func (*Store) ChangeStream() (changes corestream.Stream, ok bool)
```

ChangeStream returns the stream the store writes its change records to — [Config](#Config).Changes — and false when it was given none (core/data/docstore.ChangeFeeder).

<a name="Store.Close"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Close](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/persist.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Close() error
```

Close folds the overlay and closes the store: every later call is StoreClosed, except Stats and Close, which returns nil. A fold that fails leaves its entries where they are — the next Open replays them — and is returned; the store closes either way.

<a name="Store.Delete"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Delete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/write.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Delete(key string) error
```

Delete removes the document stored under key, or returns DocumentNotFound. Its versions go with it: a deletion never reaches the trash, which is Trash's.

<a name="Store.Documents"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Documents](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/page.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Documents(after string, limit int) iter.Seq2[coredocstore.EntryValue, error]
```

Documents yields the documents whose key sorts after after, in key order, each with its key and a copy of its JSON, at most limit of them — every one when limit is not positive — as core/data/docstore.Pager says. Each page is taken under the read lock: the next keys above the last one yielded, chosen without sorting the store, so a page costs its own documents and a pass over the keys, never a copy of them all. A write made during the listing is seen when its key sorts after the last key read. A closed store yields StoreClosed once.

<a name="Store.Entries"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Entries](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Entries(limit int) ([]coredocstore.EntryValue, error)
```

Entries returns up to limit stored documents as JSON, in key order — every one when limit is not positive — for a caller that shows documents rather than decoding them. Each JSON is the caller's own copy.

<a name="Store.Filter"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Filter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Filter(keep func(T) bool) ([]T, error)
```

Filter returns the documents keep accepts, in key order. It decodes every document; an index is the way not to.

<a name="Store.Find"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Find](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Find(index string, key string) ([]T, error)
```

Find returns the documents filed under key in the index named index, in store-key order. It reads any index, unique or not, and no document is an empty slice, not an error.

<a name="Store.FindAfter"></a>
### func \(Store\) [FindAfter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/page.go>)

```go
func (*Store) FindAfter(index string, key string, after string, limit int) iter.Seq2[T, error]
```

FindAfter yields the documents filed under key in the index named index whose store key sorts after after, in store-key order, at most limit of them — every one when limit is not positive —, each decoded as it is yielded. The holders are taken under the read lock when the range starts. IndexUnknown for an undeclared index, StoreClosed after Close.

<a name="Store.Fold"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Fold](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/persist.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Fold() error
```

Fold rewrites the snapshot with every document and removes the overlay entries it now contains. A write folds by itself when the overlay has grown enough, and Open and Close fold; Fold is for a caller that wants the resting state now — before a backup, say. A memory store has nothing to fold.

<a name="Store.Get"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Get](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Get(key string) (T, error)
```

Get returns the document stored under key, or DocumentNotFound.

<a name="Store.GetInto"></a>
### func \(Store\) [GetInto](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) GetInto(key string, dst *T) error
```

GetInto decodes the document stored under key into dst, as core/data/docstore.IntoGetter says: dst set to T's zero value first, so it ends up equal to what Get returns and shares nothing with the store or with what it held, without the fresh T Get returns. DocumentNotFound, StoreClosed or DocumentUndecodable as Get, dst zero then.

<a name="Store.Insert"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Insert](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/write.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Insert(v T) error
```

Insert stores v, which must be new: DocumentExists when its key is taken.

<a name="Store.InsertStamped"></a>
### func \(Store\) [InsertStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) InsertStamped(v T, stamp coredocstore.StampValue) error
```

InsertStamped is Insert, with what the write says about the version it makes: version 1, whatever stamp.InPlace says — or, under the key of a document in the trash, a write over that document.

<a name="Store.Keys"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Keys](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Keys(after string) iter.Seq2[string, error]
```

Keys yields the key of every document the store holds that sorts after after — every key when after is empty — in key order, and no document. The keys are taken once, under the read lock, when the range starts: a write made during the range is not seen by it. What it costs is the keys' sort, never a document's copy. A closed store yields StoreClosed once.

<a name="Store.List"></a>
### func \(Store\) [List](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) List() ([]T, error)
```

List returns every document, in key order.

<a name="Store.Lookup"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Lookup](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Lookup(index string, key string) (T, error)
```

Lookup returns the document holding key in the unique index named index, DocumentNotFound when none does, IndexUnknown for an undeclared index and IndexNotUnique for an index that may hold several: read that one with Find.

<a name="Store.OnDelete"></a>
### func \(Store\) [OnDelete](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/hooks.go>)

```go
func (*Store) OnDelete(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
```

OnDelete registers fn to be told the key of every document Delete or Trash removed, on the same terms as OnWrite.

<a name="Store.OnWrite"></a>
### func \(Store\) [OnWrite](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/hooks.go>)

```go
func (*Store) OnWrite(fn func(key string)) (remove func())
```

OnWrite registers fn to be told the key of every document Put, Insert, Replace, Update or Restore stored, once the write is durable, on the writer's goroutine and outside every lock. It returns the function that removes the registration. A panic in fn reaches the writer after its write stood.

<a name="Store.Purge"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Purge](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/trash.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Purge(key string) error
```

Purge empties the trash of the document trashed under key: the trashed document and every version it kept go, in one durable write, and a document written later under the key starts again at version 1. It calls no hook and asks Held nothing, as Delete does not. DocumentNotTrashed when no document is trashed under key.

<a name="Store.Put"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Put](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/write.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Put(v T) error
```

Put stores v under its key, creating it or replacing whatever was there. On a store that keeps versions, it makes one, stamped with nothing.

<a name="Store.PutDocument"></a>
### func \(Store\) [PutDocument](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) PutDocument(key string, versions []coredocstore.VersionValue, trashedAt time.Time) error
```

PutDocument writes the document key with its versions as they are given, in one durable write under the writers' lock, as core/data/docstore.VersionWriter says: the current version and the former ones with their numbers, instants and metadata, and — when trashedAt is set — the document in the trash at that instant. Stored, it is filed and OnWrite is told; trashed, it is neither. DocumentExists when anything is under key, VersionsInvalid, DocumentUndecodable or UniqueKeyTaken for what cannot be written as given, VersionsNotKept on a store that keeps none; nothing changes on a refusal.

<a name="Store.PutStamped"></a>
### func \(Store\) [PutStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) PutStamped(v T, stamp coredocstore.StampValue) error
```

PutStamped is Put, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="Store.Range"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Range](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/page.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Range(index string, lo string, hi string, limit int) iter.Seq2[T, error]
```

Range yields the documents filed in the ordered index named index under a key from lo, included, to hi, excluded — no upper bound when hi is empty — in index-key order, then store-key order, at most limit of them — every one when limit is not positive —, each decoded as it is yielded, and no other. The index keeps its entries sorted, so the range is a binary search and a walk, taken under the read lock when the range starts. IndexUnknown for an undeclared index, IndexNotOrdered for one declared without Ordered, StoreClosed after Close.

<a name="Store.Replace"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Replace](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/write.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Replace(v T) error
```

Replace stores v over the document already under its key: DocumentNotFound when there is none, so a document deleted meanwhile is never brought back.

<a name="Store.ReplaceIf"></a>
### func \(Store\) [ReplaceIf](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/revision.go>)

```go
func (*Store) ReplaceIf(v T, rev coredocstore.RevisionValue) error
```

ReplaceIf stores v over the document under its key, as Replace does, when that document's revision is still rev — compared under the writers' lock, which the write then keeps. RevisionMismatch otherwise, DocumentNotFound when there is no document.

<a name="Store.ReplaceStamped"></a>
### func \(Store\) [ReplaceStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) ReplaceStamped(v T, stamp coredocstore.StampValue) error
```

ReplaceStamped is Replace, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="Store.Restore"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Restore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/trash.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Restore(key string) error
```

Restore brings the document trashed under key back exactly as it was — the same JSON, the same current version — files it again and calls OnWrite. DocumentNotTrashed when no document is trashed under key, UniqueKeyTaken when another document took one of its unique keys meanwhile, DocumentUndecodable when it no longer decodes into the store's type; nothing changes on a refusal.

<a name="Store.Revision"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Revision](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/revision.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Revision(key string) (T, coredocstore.RevisionValue, error)
```

Revision returns the document stored under key and its revision — the SHA-256 of its JSON as json.Marshal writes it, so a fold, a reopen or the memory store leave it unchanged — read under the read lock. DocumentNotFound when no document is stored under key.

<a name="Store.RewriteVersions"></a>
### func \(Store\) [RewriteVersions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) RewriteVersions(key string, fn func(former []coredocstore.VersionValue) ([]coredocstore.VersionValue, error)) error
```

RewriteVersions rewrites the former versions of the document stored under key — every version but the current one, which is the document and which only a write changes — in one durable write, under the writers' lock. fn receives copies of them, newest first, and returns those to keep, in the same order: it may drop a version, and change the document one holds and what its writer said, and nothing else — VersionsRewriteRefused for a version it was not given, out of order, made at another instant or that is not JSON. An error from fn is returned as it is and changes nothing. It calls no hook: the document did not change.

It is what an erasure needs: the former versions cleared as the document is, or dropped. fn runs under the writers' lock, like Update's.

<a name="Store.Stats"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Stats](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/docstore.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Stats() StatsValue
```

Stats reports what the store holds and where its overlay stands. It answers after Close too, with the state the store closed in.

<a name="Store.Tombstones"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Tombstones](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/trash.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Tombstones() ([]coredocstore.TombstoneValue, error)
```

Tombstones returns every document in the trash, in key order: its key and the instant it was trashed. It reads every document's versions, as List reads every document.

<a name="Store.Trash"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Trash](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/trash.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Trash(key string) error
```

Trash moves the document stored under key to the trash, in one durable write under the writers' lock: it leaves every read and its index keys are freed, while its versions are kept beside the trashed document and the instant it was trashed. It calls OnDelete. DocumentNotFound when no document is stored under key, VersionsNotKept when the store keeps no versions: only a store that keeps versions has a trash.

<a name="Store.Update"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Update](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/write.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Update(key string, fn func(*T) error) (T, error)
```

Update applies fn to a copy of the document stored under key and stores the result, atomically with respect to every other write. An error from fn is returned as it is and changes nothing, and so does a result whose key is not key (DocumentKeyChanged). It returns the stored result.

fn runs under the writers' lock: it may read this store, and must not write to it — the write would wait for the lock fn holds, forever.

<a name="Store.UpdateStamped"></a>
### func \(Store\) [UpdateStamped](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) UpdateStamped(key string, stamp coredocstore.StampValue, fn func(*T) error) (T, error)
```

UpdateStamped is Update, with what the write says about the version it makes.

<a name="Store.Version"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Version](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Version(key string, number uint64) (coredocstore.VersionValue, error)
```

Version returns the version numbered number of the document stored under key, VersionNotFound when the document keeps none of that number — never made, or pruned — and what Versions returns otherwise.

<a name="Store.VersionWeight"></a>
### func \(Store\) [VersionWeight](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) VersionWeight() (coredocstore.VersionWeightValue, error)
```

VersionWeight reports what the store keeps beyond its documents — its former versions, its trashed documents and the bytes of their JSON — as core/data/docstore.VersionWeigher says. It reads the counter every write moves, which Stats also reports, and no document. VersionsNotKept on a store that keeps none, StoreClosed after Close.

<a name="Store.Versions"></a>
### func \(Store\) [Versions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/data/docstore/version.go>)

```go
func (*Store) Versions(key string) ([]coredocstore.VersionValue, error)
```

Versions returns the versions the store keeps of the document stored under key, newest first: the current one — the document as it is now — then the former ones; a document in the trash answers the versions it kept, the trashed document first. It returns DocumentNotFound when no document is stored or trashed under key, and VersionsNotKept when the store keeps no versions.

<a name="Trashable"></a>
## type [Trashable](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Trashable is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection](#Collection) that keeps a document's trash without a context, which [Store](#Store) implements: Trash, Restore, Purge and Tombstones.

```go
type Trashable = coredocstore.Trashable
```

Trashable is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.Trashable`, declared as:

```go
type Trashable interface {
	// Purge empties the trash of the document trashed under key: the
	// trashed document and every version it kept go, and a document written
	// later under the key starts again at version 1. It calls no hook — the
	// document already left every read — and asks no hold, as Delete does
	// not. DOCUMENT_NOT_TRASHED when no document is trashed under key.
	Purge(key string) error
	// Restore brings the document trashed under key back, exactly as it was
	// — the same JSON, the same current version — and files it again. It
	// calls OnWrite. DOCUMENT_NOT_TRASHED when no document is trashed under
	// key, UNIQUE_KEY_TAKEN when another document took one of its unique
	// keys meanwhile, which then stays in the trash.
	Restore(key string) error
	// Tombstones returns every document in the trash, in key order: its key
	// and when it was trashed, for a caller that empties the trash after a
	// while.
	Tombstones() ([]TombstoneValue, error)
	// Trash moves the document stored under key to the trash: it is gone from
	// every read and its index keys are freed, while its versions are kept
	// and the trash records the instant. It calls OnDelete.
	// DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND when no document is stored under key.
	Trash(key string) error
}
```

<a name="Trashable.Purge"></a>
### func \(Trashable\) [Purge](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/docstore/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Trashable) Purge(key string) error
```

Purge empties the trash of the document trashed under key: the trashed document and every version it kept go, and a document written later under the key starts again at version 1. It calls no hook — the document already left every read — and asks no hold, as Delete does not. DOCUMENT\_NOT\_TRASHED when no document is trashed under key.

<a name="Trashable.Restore"></a>

```go
func (Trashable) Restore(key string) error
```

Restore brings the document trashed under key back, exactly as it was — the same JSON, the same current version — and files it again. It calls OnWrite. DOCUMENT\_NOT\_TRASHED when no document is trashed under key, UNIQUE\_KEY\_TAKEN when another document took one of its unique keys meanwhile, which then stays in the trash.

<a name="Trashable.Tombstones"></a>

```go
func (Trashable) Tombstones() ([]TombstoneValue, error)
```

Tombstones returns every document in the trash, in key order: its key and when it was trashed, for a caller that empties the trash after a while.

<a name="Trashable.Trash"></a>
### func \(Trashable\) [Trash](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/docstore/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Trashable) Trash(key string) error
```

Trash moves the document stored under key to the trash: it is gone from every read and its index keys are freed, while its versions are kept and the trash records the instant. It calls OnDelete. DOCUMENT\_NOT\_FOUND when no document is stored under key.

<a name="Version"></a>
## type [Version](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

Version is the public alias for one version of a document: its Number from 1, the instant At the write that made it ran, the Meta that write carried, and the document as JSON.

```go
type Version = coredocstore.VersionValue
```

Version is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.VersionValue`, declared as:

```go
type Version struct {
	// At is when the write that made the version ran, in UTC, read from the
	// store's clock and kept to the nanosecond — by the file engine for the
	// years 0 to 9999, which RFC 3339 writes, and by the SQL engine for any
	// instant. It is zero for the first version of a document the store held
	// before it kept versions: when that one was written is not known.
	At     time.Time
	// Meta is what the write's caller said about it — who made it, which
	// command — as its [StampValue] gave it; nil when it said nothing. The
	// store keeps it and never reads it.
	Meta   map[string]string
	// JSON is the document as the version holds it, compact, a copy the
	// caller owns. The newest version's is the document itself.
	JSON   json.RawMessage
	// Number counts a document's versions from 1. No number is given twice
	// while the document exists or is in the trash, pruning included; a
	// document deleted, or purged from the trash, and written again is a new
	// document, and starts again at 1.
	Number uint64
}
```


<a name="VersionWriter"></a>
## type [VersionWriter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/data/docstore/gen_facade.go>)

VersionWriter is the public alias for the sibling of [Collection](#Collection) that writes a document with its versions — numbers, instants, metadata — and its trash as they are given, which [Store](#Store) implements: PutDocument. A copy from one engine to another needs it.

```go
type VersionWriter = coredocstore.VersionWriter
```

VersionWriter is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/data/docstore.VersionWriter`, declared as:

```go
type VersionWriter interface {
	// PutDocument writes the document key with versions, newest first as
	// [Versioned].Versions returns them: the current version — the document
	// itself — then the former ones, each kept as given, its number, its
	// instant (zero for a version 1 made before its store kept versions),
	// its metadata and its JSON, compacted and HTML-escaped as json.Marshal
	// writes a document. With trashedAt zero the document is stored and
	// filed in every index, and OnWrite is told; with trashedAt set, the
	// document is put in the trash at that instant, filed nowhere, and no
	// hook is told. Read back, Versions and Tombstones answer what was
	// given.
	//
	// Nothing may be under key: a document, a trashed one, or versions —
	// DOCUMENT_EXISTS otherwise. VERSIONS_INVALID, its "problem" field
	// naming which, refuses no version, a number 0, numbers that do not
	// strictly decrease, an unknown instant on a version other than 1, a
	// version that is not JSON, and a current document whose own key is not
	// key; DOCUMENT_UNDECODABLE one the store's type does not decode, and
	// UNIQUE_KEY_TAKEN a stored document whose unique key another holds. It
	// asks Held nothing and prunes nothing: the versions are written as
	// given, and the next write prunes as every write does. A refusal
	// writes nothing.
	PutDocument(key string, versions []VersionValue, trashedAt time.Time) error
}
```

<a name="VersionWriter.PutDocument"></a>
### func \(VersionWriter\) [PutDocument](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/docstore/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (VersionWriter) PutDocument(key string, versions []VersionValue, trashedAt time.Time) error
```

PutDocument writes the document key with versions, newest first as [Versioned](#Versioned).Versions returns them: the current version — the document itself — then the former ones, each kept as given, its number, its instant (zero for a version 1 made before its store kept versions), its metadata and its JSON, compacted and HTML-escaped as json.Marshal writes a document. With trashedAt zero the document is stored and filed in every index, and OnWrite is told; with trashedAt set, the document is put in the trash at that instant, filed nowhere, and no hook is told. Read back, Versions and Tombstones answer what was given.

Nothing may be under key: a document, a trashed one, or versions — DOCUMENT\_EXISTS otherwise. VERSIONS\_INVALID, its "problem" field naming which, refuses no version, a number 0, numbers that do not strictly decrease, an unknown instant on a version other than 1, a version that is not JSON, and a current document whose own key is not key; DOCUMENT\_UNDECODABLE one the store's type does not decode, and UNIQUE\_KEY\_TAKEN a stored document whose unique key another holds. It asks Held nothing and prunes nothing: the versions are written as given, and the next write prunes as every write does. A refusal writes nothing.

Version returns the version numbered number of the document stored under key: VERSION\_NOT\_FOUND when the document keeps none of that number — never made, or pruned.

<a name="Versioned.Versions"></a>
### func \(Versioned\) [Versions](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/data/docstore/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (Versioned) Versions(key string) ([]VersionValue, error)
```

Versions returns the versions kept of the document stored under key, newest first: the current one — the document as it is now — then the former ones. A document in the trash answers the versions it kept, the trashed document first. DOCUMENT\_NOT\_FOUND when no document is stored or trashed under key.
